{
  "schema_version": "evidence_intent_extraction_v1",

  "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
  "draft_intents": [
    {
      "draft_id": "D0001",
      "locator": "page 9",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "experienced an uneven economic and labor-market recovery",
      "mechanism": "employment increased and un- and under-employment decreased, while output recovered at different rates across sectors",
      "outcome": "many goods-producing and some service sectors exceeded pre-pandemic output, construction and some other sectors remained below it, and the estimated output gap narrowed from about negative 2.5 percent in early 2021 to nearly closed by mid-2022",
      "dates": ["early 2021", "mid-2022"],
      "quantities": ["output gap about -2.5 percent in early 2021"],
      "attribution": "IMF staff estimate",
      "period_fit": "Directly covers economic conditions during AMLO's 2022 ruler-period, while including an early-2021 baseline.",
      "limitations": "The IMF attributes the narrowing output gap to both recovery and temporarily below-pre-pandemic potential-output growth; the passage does not isolate the ruler's causal contribution.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.10", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0002",
      "locator": "page 9",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "increased fuel subsidies during the 2021-2022 inflation surge",
      "mechanism": "subsidies moderated energy-price inflation",
      "outcome": "energy-price inflation moderated after its initial 2021 surge, but headline inflation still rose from about 3 percent at end-2020 to 7.4 percent at end-2021 and 8.7 percent in August 2022",
      "dates": ["end-2020", "2021", "end-2021", "August 2022"],
      "quantities": [
        "headline inflation about 3 percent at end-2020",
        "headline inflation 7.4 percent at end-2021",
        "headline inflation 8.7 percent in August 2022"
      ],
      "attribution": "IMF report",
      "period_fit": "Directly covers the authorities' inflation response and outcomes through August 2022.",
      "limitations": "The passage identifies moderation in energy-price inflation but does not quantify the subsidy cost or establish the ruler's personal role.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.9", "8B.6", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0003",
      "locator": "page 81",
      "start_segment_id": "S00004",
      "end_segment_id": "S00008",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "analyzed the principal causes of Mexico's 2021-2022 headline-inflation surge",
      "mechanism": "a Phillips-curve analysis attributed much of the increase first to energy and food prices and later also to residual cost-push factors",
      "outcome": "rising energy and food prices explained much of the inflation surge through the third quarter of 2021 and much of subsequent above-target inflation, while residual pressures contributed especially in the first quarter of 2022",
      "dates": ["2021-2022", "through 2021Q3", "2022Q1"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff empirical analysis",
      "period_fit": "Provides contemporaneous causal context for inflation during the 2022 ruler-period.",
      "limitations": "This is model-based analysis; it mainly concerns external and cost-push drivers and does not attribute inflation outcomes to the ruler.",
      "polarity": "contextual",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0004",
      "locator": "page 83",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "proposed fiscal-framework reforms to replenish fiscal buffers for 2023",
      "mechanism": "the proposals repurposed resources within a context of depleted contingencies, limited room in the 2022 and 2023 budgets, and mounting 2023 downside risks",
      "outcome": "the IMF characterized the approach as quick and efficient for immediate risks but as increasing complexity and doing little to improve reliability or correct fiscal policy's pro-cyclical bias",
      "dates": ["2020", "2022", "2023"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "The reform proposal arose in 2022 and concerned fiscal preparedness for 2023.",
      "limitations": "This passage concerns proposals rather than completed enactment or observed shock-response outcomes.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "8B.1", "8B.2", "8B.8", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0005",
      "locator": "page 83",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00008",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "used stabilization funds to support the budget during the pandemic-era revenue shortfall",
      "mechanism": "0.9 percent of GDP was transferred from stabilization funds in 2020 after a 0.5-percent-of-GDP transfer in 2019",
      "outcome": "the funds were almost depleted, with only 0.2 percent of GDP remaining, and 2022 oil-revenue surprises were considered unlikely to replenish them amid rising downside risks",
      "dates": ["2019", "2020", "2022"],
      "quantities": [
        "2019 transfer: 0.5 percent of GDP",
        "2020 transfer: 0.9 percent of GDP",
        "remaining balance: 0.2 percent of GDP"
      ],
      "attribution": "IMF report",
      "period_fit": "The depletion largely predates 2022 but materially defines the fiscal capacity inherited within the target year.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not separate discretionary ruler choices from automatic or institutional fiscal mechanisms.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7", "8B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0006",
      "locator": "page 83",
      "start_segment_id": "S00009",
      "end_segment_id": "S00016",
      "actor": "Mexico's federal fiscal framework",
      "action": "used the Mexican Petroleum Fund to collect oil revenues, finance the federal budget, fund stabilization accounts, and hold long-term reserves",
      "mechanism": "law required transfers matching budgeted oil revenue and then specified contributions of up to 2.22 percent and 0.64 percent of projected oil revenue to federal and state stabilization funds before long-term reserve accumulation",
      "outcome": "long-term reserves had remained near USD 1 billion since 2018, while transfers to the federal government were expected to rise from MEX$364 billion in 2021 to MEX$673 billion in 2022",
      "dates": ["since 2018", "2021", "2022"],
      "quantities": [
        "federal stabilization contribution cap: 2.22 percent of projected oil revenue",
        "state stabilization contribution cap: 0.64 percent of projected oil revenue",
        "long-term reserves: about USD 1 billion",
        "long-term reserves: 0.07 percent of 2022 GDP",
        "2021 federal transfer: MEX$364 billion or 1.4 percent of GDP",
        "expected 2022 federal transfer: MEX$673 billion or 2.3 percent of GDP"
      ],
      "attribution": "IMF description of the statutory framework",
      "period_fit": "Describes the fiscal institution and expected 2022 resource flows under the target-period government.",
      "limitations": "The passage describes standing legal mechanisms and projections, not a ruler-specific decision or final executed 2022 amount.",
      "polarity": "contextual",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "8B.2", "8B.3", "8B.6"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0007",
      "locator": "page 84",
      "start_segment_id": "S00003",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006",
      "actor": "Mexico's Budget Revenue Stabilization Fund",
      "action": "received oil-hedging, petroleum-fund, and investment-return financing while covering a major 2020 budget revenue shortfall",
      "mechanism": "the fund received MEX$47 billion from oil hedging, MEX$9 billion from petroleum-fund transfers, and MEX$9 billion from asset returns, then transferred MEX$157 billion to the budget",
      "outcome": "its balance fell from MEX$158 billion in 2019 to MEX$9.5 billion at end-2020; inflows were MEX$7.5 billion in 2021 and expected at MEX$8 billion in 2022",
      "dates": ["2019", "2020", "end-2020", "2021", "2022"],
      "quantities": [
        "2020 oil-hedging inflow: MEX$47 billion or 0.2 percent of GDP",
        "2020 petroleum-fund inflow: MEX$9 billion or 0.04 percent of GDP",
        "2020 asset-return inflow: MEX$9 billion or 0.04 percent of GDP",
        "2020 budget transfer: MEX$157 billion or 0.7 percent of GDP",
        "2019 balance: MEX$158 billion or 0.6 percent of GDP",
        "end-2020 balance: MEX$9.5 billion or 0.04 percent of GDP",
        "2021 inflow: MEX$7.5 billion or 0.01 percent of GDP",
        "expected 2022 inflow: MEX$8 billion or 0.03 percent of GDP"
      ],
      "attribution": "IMF report",
      "period_fit": "Provides the institutional and quantitative baseline for 2022 shock-response capacity.",
      "limitations": "Most depletion occurred in 2020; the 2022 transfer figure was an expectation rather than a final outturn.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.3", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0008",
      "locator": "page 84",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00010",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities and existing fiscal-financing mechanisms",
      "action": "used oil-revenue gains for fuel-related budget pressures rather than rebuilding fiscal contingencies",
      "mechanism": "windfall oil revenues collected by the petroleum fund were increasingly absorbed by the budget, leaving little or nothing to replenish the stabilization fund or build petroleum-fund reserves",
      "outcome": "the stabilization fund held MEX$25 billion at end-June 2022 against an authority-estimated MEX$100 billion adequate contingency for 2023, and expected 2022 transfers were only another 0.03 percent of GDP",
      "dates": ["end-June 2022", "2022", "2023"],
      "quantities": [
        "authority-estimated adequate contingency: MEX$100 billion",
        "adequate contingency: 0.35 percent of 2022 GDP and 0.33 percent of 2023 GDP",
        "end-June 2022 balance: MEX$25 billion or 0.09 percent of 2022 GDP",
        "expected additional 2022 transfers: 0.03 percent of GDP"
      ],
      "attribution": "IMF report, including the Mexican authorities' adequacy estimate",
      "period_fit": "Directly concerns resource allocation and shock preparedness in 2022.",
      "limitations": "The passage links resource use to fuel-related spending pressure but does not establish a personal directive by the ruler.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.3", "8B.7", "8B.9"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0009",
      "locator": "page 84",
      "start_segment_id": "S00011",
      "end_segment_id": "S00013",
      "actor": "Mexico's oil-based fiscal contingency system",
      "action": "relied on declining oil production and an oil hedge not directly linked to the economic cycle",
      "mechanism": "a smaller oil-revenue base reduced residual funds available after contingencies were used, while the hedge did not operate automatically with cyclical conditions",
      "outcome": "the IMF found that these mechanisms might not supply sufficient resources for future counter-cyclical policy or function as an automatic fiscal stabilizer",
      "dates": ["future period assessed in the 2022 report"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Assesses structural limitations evident during 2022 and their implications beyond the year.",
      "limitations": "This is a prospective institutional assessment rather than an observed policy failure during a specific shock.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10", "8B.7", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0010",
      "locator": "page 85",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006",
      "actor": "Mexican government",
      "action": "proposed a new debt-issuance-based mechanism to finance the Budget Revenue Stabilization Fund in its 2023 budget package",
      "mechanism": "unused annual debt-issuance headroom would become a government IOU deposited in the fund, which the fund could dispose of or exchange in the next fiscal year to obtain liquidity",
      "outcome": "the proposal would permit the fund to hold financial assets, initially government paper and potentially other instruments, while continuing to prohibit it from incurring financial liabilities",
      "dates": ["2023 budget package", "next fiscal year"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF description of the government's proposed reforms",
      "period_fit": "The proposal was made in the 2022 ruler-period for the 2023 budget framework.",
      "limitations": "The cited passage describes a proposal, not ratification, implementation, or realized financing.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "8B.1", "8B.2", "8B.6"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0011",
      "locator": "page 85",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00013",
      "actor": "Mexican government's proposed fiscal reform",
      "action": "diversified stabilization-fund financing away from oil by adding debt issuance",
      "mechanism": "the new mechanism broadened the financing base and could be used before shocks occurred, avoiding exclusive reliance on petroleum-fund transfers or oil put options",
      "outcome": "the IMF assessed that diversification would reduce vulnerability to oil-price and production trends and mitigate the trade-off between funding contingencies and immediate spending, while existing oil mechanisms were constrained and generally could not build buffers before a shock",
      "dates": ["2022 proposal", "future shocks"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Assesses the design of a reform proposed during 2022.",
      "limitations": "Expected benefits were prospective and contingent on enactment and implementation.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "8B.2", "8B.8", "8B.9", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0012",
      "locator": "page 85",
      "start_segment_id": "S00014",
      "end_segment_id": "S00017",
      "actor": "Mexican government's proposed fiscal reform",
      "action": "retained much of the existing framework to permit rapid implementation before near-term 2023 downside risks",
      "mechanism": "ratification before the end of 2022 was expected to release MEX$20-30 billion for the stabilization fund",
      "outcome": "the IMF judged the proposal a pragmatic step that could materially support contingencies if 2023 risks materialized, while also stating that comprehensive reform remained necessary for flexibility, reliability, transparency, and fiscal responsibility",
      "dates": ["before end-2022", "2023"],
      "quantities": ["expected stabilization-fund resources: MEX$20-30 billion"],
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Directly evaluates the timing and expected near-term effect of a 2022 reform proposal.",
      "limitations": "The financing and support were expected, not observed; the passage conditions them on ratification and future risk realization.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "8B.2", "8B.6", "8B.9", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0013",
      "locator": "page 86",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00003",
      "actor": "Mexican government's proposed fiscal reform",
      "action": "used year-end debt-ceiling headroom as the basis for additional stabilization-fund financing",
      "mechanism": "funding depended on the uncertain amount of unused debt authorization remaining at year-end",
      "outcome": "the IMF found that the approach increased complexity, weakened transparency, made financing uncertain and unreliable, and left the current framework's pro-cyclical bias unaddressed",
      "dates": ["year-end under the proposed framework"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Evaluates limitations of the reform proposed during 2022.",
      "limitations": "The assessment concerns design risks rather than observed post-enactment performance.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "8B.2", "8B.7", "8B.8", "8B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0014",
      "locator": "page 87",
      "start_segment_id": "S00006",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007",
      "actor": "Mexico's existing fiscal framework",
      "action": "required a cash-balanced budget subject to specified exclusions and broad public-sector coverage",
      "mechanism": "the balanced-budget rule covered the federal government, PEMEX, CFE, social-security institutions, and various trust funds while excluding PEMEX investment from the cash-balance requirement",
      "outcome": "the IMF characterized the rule as broadly pro-cyclical",
      "dates": ["current framework at the time of the 2022 report"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF description and assessment",
      "period_fit": "Describes a fiscal rule operating during 2022.",
      "limitations": "This is an inherited statutory framework; the passage does not specify whether AMLO created or modified it.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "8B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0015",
      "locator": "page 87",
      "start_segment_id": "S00020",
      "end_segment_id": "S00023",
      "actor": "Mexico's fiscal framework",
      "action": "allowed escape clauses requiring justification of the deficit, financing amount, return period, and corrective measures",
      "mechanism": "the clauses were activated repeatedly during 2010-2012 and 2014-2016",
      "outcome": "the framework was respected in only seven of the thirteen years through 2020, with IMF analysis identifying its inflexibility as a key factor",
      "dates": ["2010-2012", "2014-2016", "through 2020"],
      "quantities": ["framework respected in 7 of 13 years through 2020"],
      "attribution": "IMF report, referring to IMF 2020",
      "period_fit": "Predates the 2022 target year and serves only as inherited-framework context.",
      "limitations": "The evidence is not specific to the ruler's 2022 conduct and cannot establish target-period implementation.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "8B.7", "8B.10"]
    }
  ],
  "locator_dispositions": [
    {

    },
    {
      "locator": "page 84",

    },
    {
      "locator": "page 85",

      "reason": "Contains the government's proposed 2023 fiscal reforms, their mechanism, expected resources, prospective benefits, and limitations."
    },
    {
      "locator": "page 86",

      "reason": "Contains IMF findings on complexity, transparency, financing uncertainty, reliability, and unresolved pro-cyclicality."
    },
    {
      "locator": "page 87",
      "disposition": "used",
      "reason": "Contains factual descriptions and assessments of current fiscal rules, including pro-cyclicality and historical compliance."
    },
    {
      "locator": "page 88",
      "disposition": "not_used",
      "reason": "Lists IMF/FSAP recommendations rather than implemented ruler actions or observed target-period outcomes."
    },
    {
      "locator": "page 89",
      "disposition": "not_used",
      "reason": "Lists prospective financial-development recommendations without evidence of government adoption or implementation."
    },
    {
      "locator": "page 9",
      "disposition": "used",
      "reason": "Contains 2022 recovery, labor-market, inflation, and fuel-subsidy facts relevant to economic shock response and outcomes."
    }
  ]
}
